newsitem.title: UK: Shell cautious on oil prices after flat Q1 profit.
newsitem.headline: Shell cautious on oil prices after flat Q1 profit.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group reported flat first quarter earnings Thursday and said oil prices might fall further from recent highs with refining margins staying under pressure.

Shell said earnings excluding special items edged up to 1.55 billion British pounds ($2.5 billion) from 1.54 billion a year earlier. Lower gas sales, higher taxes and the pound's strength offset higher oil production profits and a strong chemical performance, the giant oil company said.
Overall earnings, which roughly met analysts' expectations, would have risen by 7 percent if measured in dollars, Shell said.

Shell's results came after U.S. oil companies last month surprised markets with strong results. But industry analysts said Shell's performance should not be taken as meaning the Anglo-Dutch group was lagging behind its U.S. rivals.
Any comparison should take into account that Shell's first quarter profits in 1996 were exceptionally high due to several one-time factors such as an unusually low tax rate.
Results also were boosted a year ago by exceptionally cold winter weather in Europe. In contrast, mild temperatures early in 1997 led to a 4 percent drop in natural gas sales volumes, Shell said.
Despite this, profits in exploration and production rose 9 percent, mainly on higher oil prices.
Refining and marketing profits fell 1 percent. Lower profits in the United States were largely offset by an improved performance elsewhere in the world, Shell said.

Chemicals earnings rose 12 percent due to cost-cutting. The chemicals recovery may continue in the second quarter, the company said, but the longer-term outlook hinged on the ability to pass on higher feedstock prices.
Shell saw scope for oil prices to fall further as worldwide production increases were likely to exceed demand growth.
Analysts were not too upset by the company's downbeat comments, saying lower crude oil prices were already factored into the market.
If anything, Shell's oil price warning showed the group's prospects were better than many of its rivals, several analysts said.

Most competitors were far more geared towards oil production than Shell and were therefore more vulnerable to to lower crude prices, they said. "If you look at Shell's position they will do better than their peers if the oil price falls further," said one analyst.
Meanwhile, shares in Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc fell 7-1/2 pence (12 cents) to 1,082-1/2 ($17.46) in late afternoon trading. Shares in Royal Dutch Petroleum edged lower in Amsterdam.
